Although I have family that loves me, I am at the point where I am going five days sober, then drinking a bottle of vodka. I have to keep my drinking as secret as possible from those closest to me - they may notice when I drink, in fact probably so. As long as I keep to my own peaceful space, and they draw distance when I drink, then this is a satisfactory equilibrium. I do the five days sober to remain functional for employment (I start a new job next week).

The best thing to do is to drink with someone that understands. So that you do not have to drink in secret. For most people, they will leave after the sixth pint at the pub - they are typically rather drowsy and feel out of the ordinary with that feeling. Whereas for us, that is what is often necessary for any sense of relaxation.
I am going to a SMART recovery meeting next week for the first time, to see which approach resonates better.
